thread.title_full: Atlanta Falcons coach makes feelings clear on Michael Penix vs Kirk Cousins debate - NewsBreak

author: Rory Robinson
title: Atlanta Falcons coach makes feelings clear on Michael Penix vs Kirk Cousins debate - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
2 hours ago The Atlanta Falcons are facing questions at quarterback after one of their ugliest defeats in years, a 30-0 embarrassment against NFC South rival Carolina Panthers, despite Michael Strahan calling Atlanta the better team .
The shutout dropped them to 1-2, and fans have already started stirring a debate about whether rookie Michael Penix Jr . is the long-term answer or if veteran Kirk Cousins should get his job back. After not showing up to voluntary training camp, Cousins has seemingly accepted the role as a backup.
Head coach Raheem Morris made it clear he has no interest in entertaining that conversation. Despite the brutal loss, Morris doubled down on his support for the No. 8 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, insisting Penix remains his starter as Atlanta prepares for a Week 4 clash against the Washington Commanders.

READ MORE: Bryson DeChambeau at Ryder Cup practice round shows why he's different to USA teammates
"Kirk lost his job last year. We’re not even close to that with Mike [Penix]," Morris said.
"He had a bad day. We had a bad day. Mike is our quarterback. We have a lot of confidence in Mike. We're moving forward with Mike. Mike's the guy."
Penix's "bad day" was the worst performance of his young NFL career. He went 18-for-36 with 172 passing yards, two interceptions, including a pick-six, and a QBR of 12.5 with no scores.
Cousins entered late in the blowout, completing 5-of-7 passes for 29 yards.
Morris dismissed the late-game switch as a practical decision.
"The game was out of hand," he said. "You move on, keep him out of harm's way. Keep our guys out of harm's way. The game's out of hand; they got us."
Penix is 25 years old and showed flashes last season when he filled in down the stretch, throwing for 775 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in five appearances. He became the starter after Cousins' decline in 2024, which saw the veteran throw 10 touchdowns to 15 interceptions , with a string of costly turnovers derailing Atlanta's playoff hopes.
The four-time Pro Bowler experienced big highs during his first year in Atlanta, including a 509-yard, four-touchdown performance against Tampa Bay, but also bottomed out with multiple multi-interception games as the Falcons limped to a losing record.
That inconsistency opened the door for Penix, whose strong preseason convinced Morris to move forward with the rookie.
The Falcons' offense has yet to take off, averaging just 14 points per game, the second-worst mark in the NFL behind only the winless Houston Texans.
However, the defense has been one of the league’s top units, allowing the second-lowest yards per game.
It leaves Atlanta in a familiar bind with a roster that looks playoff-worthy everywhere but at quarterback. Penix gets another chance to prove he belongs on Sunday against Washington.
A bounce-back performance could cool the debate, but another rough outing would only turn up the noise on a controversy that Morris is trying to silence before it gets started.
